History:
- Chief complaint: New dry, itchy, red skin on arms and hands.
- Onset/duration: Began a few days ago.
- Course: Persistent; not improved with coconut butter.
- Distribution: Mainly hands and arms; patient denied spread to chest/legs/face (per consult).
- Associated symptoms: Itch; redness. Denies fever, sweating, vomiting, diarrhea, “spots,” or skin bleeding/discharge. Reports feeling tired.
- Triggers/context: Symptoms started after swimming a few days ago. Recent increased work-related stress (primary school teacher, long hours).
- Self-care: Coconut butter for several days without relief.
- Systemic review: Eating/drinking normally; bowels and urination normal.

Past Medical History:
- No prior skin conditions (no history of eczema/dermatitis).
- Possible lactose intolerance (patient-reported).
- Family history: Father with asthma; mother with hay fever; no known family skin disorders.
- Medications: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) — dose/route/frequency not documented. No other medications reported.
- Allergies: No drug or food allergies documented; possible lactose intolerance noted.
- Social: Lives alone; non-smoker; does not drink alcohol; no recreational drug use; works as a primary school teacher.

Physical Examination:
- No in-person exam performed (teleconsult).
- Reported findings: Red, dry, itchy skin on hands and arms. No fever. No “spots.” No sweating. No skin bleeding or discharge reported. Patient otherwise well.

Impression:
- Acute dermatitis of the hands and arms, likely irritant/contact dermatitis (onset after swimming), with stress as a possible contributing factor; no systemic features.

Management Plan:
- Education: Provided dermatitis patient information leaflet.
- Topical therapy: Recommended topical corticosteroid cream for inflammation (specific agent/strength not documented).
- Skin care: Frequent liberal use of emollients throughout the day for the next few days.
- Symptom control: Over-the-counter antihistamines (e.g., chlorpheniramine [Piriton], loratadine) for itch.
- Analgesia: Painkillers (e.g., acetaminophen) not indicated for itch in this case.
- Follow-up: Return in 1 week if not improving for reassessment.

Patient Summary:
- 26-year-old with new-onset pruritic, erythematous, dry rash on hands/arms beginning a few days after swimming, without systemic symptoms. Clinical picture consistent with acute contact/irritant dermatitis. Plan includes emollients, topical steroid, OTC antihistamines, and short-interval follow-up.

Key Takeaways:
- Apply emollients frequently to affected areas.
- Use the prescribed/recommended topical steroid as directed for a few days to reduce inflammation.
- Consider OTC antihistamines to reduce itching.

Next Steps:
- Monitor symptoms over the next few days; arrange follow-up next week if not improving.
- No tests ordered at this visit.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No in-person skin exam; no description of lesion morphology (e.g., plaques, scaling, fissures), exact distribution, or presence of excoriations; no documentation of drug allergies beyond lactose intolerance; specific topical steroid name/strength/dose and emollient regimen not documented; no counseling documented on potential irritant avoidance (e.g., pool chemicals, harsh soaps).
- Internal conflicts: Patient initially stated “not on any medication” but later confirmed taking Microgynon (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Some inaudible/elliptical segments; clinician inferred some answers (e.g., lack of spread), but overall history understandable.
